title: 情報処理心理学
subtitle: Psychology of Information Processing
educationalGoal: Through reflecting on daily cognitive activities and connecting them with the theories covered in the class, students will: - be able to understand the characteristics of human information processing systems. - be able to understand the characteristics of human information processing systems in contrast to computer information processing.
advice: This course will focus on the contents of cognitive psychology, which is an area of psychology that captures human cognitive functions as information processing systems. Cognitive psychology has been developed by using a conceptual device called information processing (using a computer metaphor). Elucidation of human “intelligence” (cognitive characteristics of human information processing) is indispensable for the realization of “intelligence” in machines such as artificial intelligence and robotics, which has attracted attention in recent years. Specifically, the following topics are covered. (1) Representation of knowledge and processing: (a) Declarative knowledge / Procedural knowledge, (b) Spatial information processing (2) Conscious processing and unconscious processing: (a) Attention, (b) Controlled processing and automatic processing (3) Encoding processes and retrieval processes: (a) Memory, (b) Levels of processing (4) Cognitive psychology and profession The above contents are learned through knowledge internalization (for example, lectures) and knowledge externalization (for example, discussions and presentations). We perform various cognitive activities in everyday life. It is desirable to understand the content of the course while being conscious of cognitive activities in daily life. #This course is required for Certified Psychologists.
requiredKnowledge: It is recommended that students understand the contents of the “Psychological Experiments and Practice of Elementary Psychological Experiments” course that was offered separately. Students should set goals to grow themselves, and not aim simply to obtain credit for the course.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Understand the characteristics of human information processing systems, express them in own words and consider their meaning. (2) Understand the characteristics of the human information processing system in contrast to computer information processing, express them in own words and consider their meaning. (3) Understand situations where knowledge of information processing psychology is utilized in the real world, and be able to increase perspectives of future career paths.
achievementLevels.standard: (1) Understand the characteristics of human information processing systems and have your own thoughts. (2) Understand the characteristics of the human information processing system in contrast to computer information processing and have your own thoughts. (3) Be aware of future career paths, understand the situations in which knowledge of information processing psychology are utilized in the real world.
